- When sentiment is high (≥0.6), model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is low (≤0.4), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to align with mean reversion bias.
- Model consistently overreacts to recent spikes (e.g., +5–10% above recent high); apply dampening factor of 0.85–0.90 to peak forecasts.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows persistent lag: true price often turns 1–2 days after model peak; adjust for 1–3 day delay in price reaction.
- If sentiment drops sharply after a spike, model fails to correct; add 1–2% downward adjustment to forecast following sentiment dip.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show downward trend, forecast should not exceed 1–2% above recent low.
- Avoid forecasting above 75% of recent 18-day high unless sentiment >0.75; otherwise, cap at 70–72% of high to prevent overshoot.
